deep.reconstruction:
Folio 75r is the first page of Riemann's philosophical fragment 'Antinomien'. It is marked '7' at top left and '(zu p. 6)' at top right. There is no mathematical derivation on the page. Its content is conceptual, and its one mathematical element is a methodological model taken from analysis.

(1) A Kant-style table of antinomies. The governing principle is THESIS = the finite, the representable (Vorstellbares). ANTITHESIS = the infinite: 'systems of concepts that lie at the limit (Grenze) of the representable'.
- I. Thesis: finite elements of time and space. Antithesis: the continuous (Stetiges).
- II. Thesis: freedom. This is defined not as Kant's power to begin a causal series absolutely, but as the power to decide between two or more given possibilities. Riemann adds a compatibilist gloss: for decision by free choice (Willkür) to be possible under completely determining laws of the action of mental representations, one must assume the following. The psychic mechanism itself has, or at least acquires in its development, the property of bringing about the necessity of that decision. Antithesis: 'Determinismus'. The gloss reads: no one, when acting, can give up the conviction that the future is co-determined by his action.
- III. Thesis: a God acting in time (world-government, Weltregierung). Antithesis: a timeless, personal, omniscient, omnipotent, all-good God (providence, Vorsehung).
- IV. Thesis: immortality. Antithesis: in Kant's vocabulary, a thing-in-itself underlying temporal development, endowed with transcendental freedom, radical evil and an intelligible character.

(2) A commentary on II/III. Freedom in the stated sense is fully compatible with strict lawfulness of nature. A timeless God, however, is not tenable alongside it. The restriction that freedom of creatures imposes on omnipotence and omniscience must be lifted by assuming a God acting in time, a 'guide of the hearts and destinies of men'. Providence must be supplemented and partly replaced by world-government.

(3) 'General relation of the concept-systems of thesis and antithesis.' The method Newton used to found the infinitesimal calculus is the method of limits (Grenzmethode). Riemann says that since the beginning of the 19th century it has been recognized by the best mathematicians as the only one giving sure results.
- Description: instead of a continuous transition from one value of a magnitude to another (or from one place, or one determination of a concept, to another), one passes through finitely many intermediate stages. One then lets the number of stages grow so that all gaps between consecutive stages tend to zero (continued on 75v).
- In modern terms (my gloss): a continuous path or quantity is treated as the limit of discrete partitions x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_n with max|x_{k+1} - x_k| -> 0, as in Riemann/Cauchy sums.
- The philosophical point, completed on the next page: the antithesis concepts are not positively representable. They are limits of representable (thesis) concept-systems, reached by changing only the 'magnitude relations'. Some mediating correlate concepts lose representability in the limit.
- Hence the antinomy is resolved structurally, on the model of finite partition -> continuum.
errors: No mathematical errors; there are no computations.

Historical remark, not an error: calling the limit method 'Newton's' is a common 19th-century view, resting on Newton's prime and ultimate ratios. The claim that it had been the only accepted rigorous foundation 'since the beginning of this century' really points to Cauchy (1821) and his school; Lagrange around 1797 had instead advocated power series.
Under II, the antithesis is labelled 'Determinismus', but its gloss states a conviction of agency. As written, the pairing of label and content is somewhat odd, possibly a compressed note.

results.what: Description of the limit method: replace a continuous transition by finitely many intermediate stages, then let their number grow so that all step sizes tend to 0
results.modern_name: Method of limits / partition refinement (as in Cauchy/Riemann integration)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (prime and ultimate ratios, 1687); made the standard foundation by Cauchy (1821)

results.what: Using the limit concept as a philosophical model: unrepresentable 'antithesis' concepts (continuum, timeless God, etc.) as limits of representable finite concept-systems
results.modern_name: Limit-concept resolution of Kantian antinomies (Riemann's philosophical fragments)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann; published in Weber/Dedekind's Gesammelte Werke under 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts: Antinomien'

results.what: Compatibilist notion of freedom (choice among given possibilities) within strict natural law, plus a temporally acting God
results.usually_credited_to: Long philosophical tradition (Leibniz, Hume; Herbart-influenced psychology)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 'Antinomien' fragment, printed in Riemann's collected works among the philosophical fragments and much discussed in Riemann/Herbart scholarship. There is no new mathematics; the limit method described is standard.

checkable.asserts: Example of the Grenzmethode: refining finitely many intermediate stages with spacing 1/n -> 0 recovers the continuous quantity; the difference is 0.
Sum of n equal step sizes from 0 to 1 tends to the total transition length 1 (difference 0).

transcription_corrections: Section II thesis: 'Denn [?] durch völlig bestimmende Gesetze ... Entscheidung durch Willkür ausgeschlossen [?] ist, so muss man annehmen' should read 'Damit durch völlig bestimmende Gesetze des Wirkens der Vorstellungen Entscheidung durch Willkür möglich sei, muss man annehmen' (the image shows 'mög-lich sei').

Section IV antithesis: the machine reading is wrong. The image reads approximately 'Ein außer aller zeitlichen Entwicklung zu Grunde liegendes Ding an sich mit transcendentaler Freiheit, radicalem Bösen, intelligiblem Charakter ausgestattet.' This uses Kantian terminology: Ding an sich, transcendentale Freiheit, radikales Böse, intelligibler Charakter.
Final paragraph of the commentary: a semicolon/new clause follows 'Geschicke der Menschen' ('; der Begriff der Vorsehung muss ergänzt ...').
Header: 'Antinomien.' has a struck initial attempt and a small cross above it; '(zu p. 6)' at top right and '7' at top left are correct; the circled folio number 75 is an archival stamp.
